newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel prepares to unveil debt plan.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel prepares to unveil debt plan.

text.p: Debt-laden channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA /Plc will later on Monday detail a plan to reduce its gigantic nine billion pounds ($14.09 billion) obligations to its bank creditors.
The deal, agreed last week, is expected to reduce the company's debt and interest bill by around half.

The banks are expected to end up with 49 percent of Eurotunnel's equity which will be swapped for two billion pounds of debt at around or slightly above the 9.5 francs per share price at which the stock was suspended last Monday.

Another portion of the debt is expected to be exchanged for a convertible bond while banks will also be able to choose other instruments which will reduce Eurotunnel's interest bill rather than the principal sum itself.
Some of these instruments could run for as long as 40 years, according to newspaper reports.
It is expected that some of the instruments will contain step-up interest payments which will depend on the company's revenues.
Interest unpaid since the company froze interest payments in September 1995 is expected to be treated separately.
Details of the deal are due to be announced at news conferences in both Paris and London at 1000 GMT.
The deal still has to meet with approval of the current shareholders and of all of the 225 creditor banks.
A group of 26 so-called "instructing" banks was shown the deal at a meeting in London on Friday.
Shareholders will vote on the restructuring at an extraordinary general meeting, probably next year. ($1=.6388 Pound)
